newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins confidence vote on refugee bill.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins confidence vote on refugee bill.

text.p: The Italian government easily won a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament on Thursday to overcome hundreds of opposition amendments to a decree on Albanian refugees in Italy.
It was the 22nd confidence vote called and won by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition during its year in office, but another do-or-die motion is expected next week.
The motion was carried by 306 votes to 192, with Prodi's hard-left parliamentary allies, the Communist Refoundation, securing the government's majortiy.
The decree, which has already been approved by the Senate (upper house), was introduced by the cabinet in March after a flood of refugees poured into Italy to escape turmoil in Albania.
It allows the Albanians to stay in Italy for 90 days after which they have to return home. It also provides financing for their upkeep while in Italy.
Under a recent constitutional court ruling, cabinet decrees will lapse unless they are converted into law within 60 days.

The refugee decree was set to expire on Monday and the government called the confidence vote after the separatist Northern League party tabled hundreds of amendments to the package and lined up its deputies to debate every point.
The League opposes the government's policy towards the Albanians, arguing that they are not genuine refugees and should therefore be immediately repatriated.

More than 15,000 Albanian refugees crossed the Adriatic Sea to Italy in a flotilla of ramshackle boats to escape anarchy and a political crisis in the wake of the collapse of hugely popular investment schemes.

Italian authorities have sent back some so-called "undesirables" while other refugees are staying in temporary accommodation around the country. Hundreds more escaped police surveillance and disappeared.

The hard-right National Alliance party said it also wanted the Albanian refugees sent home before their 90 days were up, but it criticised the huge mass of League amendments, saying that they had prevented a serious debate on the issue.
The leader of the Senate budget committee said the government would probably call a confidence vote in the upper house next week on its mini-budget in order to sidestep opposition filibustering.

"The Northern League party is continuing its sterile obstructionism, sticking to its 400 amendments, making it very hard to vote on the whole package in a single day," Romualdo Coviello told reporters.

The mini-budget decree is due to expire on May 28 and the government wants the Senate to approve the bill on May 22. Prodi's coalition has a clear majority in the upper house and does not need Refoundation support.
The Northern League, which last year proclaimed symbolic independence for the north of Italy, has taken to obstructing most government decrees in a bid to snarl parliamentary activity.
